blocks.text: The seed parables use familiar processes—sowing across varied ground, growth, weeds, harvest, and garden plants—so their comparisons are concrete rather than abstract. This helps clarify the imagery while preserving the parables’ literary function. The boat scenes likewise involve a recognizably workable lake craft: a preserved wooden boat found near Ginosar, dating broadly from about 100 BCE to 100 CE, was roughly eight meters long and constructed and repaired from multiple timbers. It offers a material comparison for the size, construction, propulsion, and repair of the boats assumed in the crossings.
